::: {.bio-column}

I study language, communication, and cognition in digital environments using computational methods. I am currently a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Institute of Computing, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), and previously worked as a Senior Research Associate at the University of Bristol. I also serve on the Editorial Board of *Communications Psychology*, and my research has appeared in journals including *Nature Human Behaviour*, *Nature Communications*, *PNAS Nexus*, *Communications Psychology*, and *EACL*.


:::

:::

:::


::: {#research .content-section}

# Research

My research examines misinformation, political communication, and the role of emerging technologies in online environments. I use computational approaches to study language and digital data, drawing on natural language processing, corpus and text analysis, statistical modelling, experiments, and large language models.

A central part of my work examines misinformation and political discourse develop and spread online. I have studied political discourse and populist language on social media, political honesty, persuasion, and the diffusion of low-quality information.

More recently, I have been extending this research to online communities and artificial intelligence. My current work includes the study of misinformation in radicalised communities on Telegram and the use of LLM-agent-based approaches to studying and intervening in online communities.
